sentence: We start with a single equilateral triangle.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the initial setup of the problem (starting with one triangle).

sentence: Because every triangle has 3 sides, the first figure (with 1 tile) has a perimeter of 3 × 7 = 21 cm.
sentence-category-reason: Computes the initial perimeter using 3 × 7 = 21 cm.

sentence: Now, when you add a new triangle, you place it so that it shares one entire side with the previous figure.
sentence-category-reason: Describes the side-sharing arrangement to set up perimeter reasoning.

sentence: That shared side is now “internal” and no longer part of the perimeter, while the new triangle contributes its two other (exposed) sides.
sentence-category-reason: Explains how a shared side becomes internal and affects perimeter.

sentence: In effect, instead of adding all 3 sides (which would add 3 × 7 cm), you lose 1 side’s worth of length (7 cm) because that side is formerly on the perimeter of the original figure.
sentence-category-reason: Conceptually analyzes the perimeter change when adding a tile.

sentence:
Thus the net increase in perimeter when you add a tile is:
  (3 new sides – 1 covered side) × 7 cm = 2 × 7 cm – 7 cm = 7 cm.
sentence-category-reason: Calculates the net perimeter increase per added tile (7 cm).

sentence:
So for a figure with n tiles, starting with 1 tile with perimeter 21 cm, the perimeter is:
  Perimeter = 21 cm + 7(n – 1).
We are told that the figure’s perimeter is 91 cm.
sentence-category-reason: Restates the given target perimeter of 91 cm.
Performs algebraic step subtracting 21 to get 7(n − 1) = 70.
Performs algebraic division to obtain n − 1 = 10.

sentence: Therefore, the figure with a perimeter of 91 cm is made of 11 tiles.
sentence-category-reason: States the final result: the figure uses 11 tiles.
